look_here_first: Start with where the flowers are. Common wild petunia sends a conspicuous peduncled, branching terminal flower stalk above the leaves; the flowers are not sitting directly in the leaf axils. Then confirm mostly glabrous/glabrescent oval-ovate leaves with wavy to low-dentate margins.

lookalikes.differences: Ruellia drummondiana: R. drummondiana bears flowers/cymes directly from leaf axils with essentially no peduncle and has short fine pubescence; its capsules contain only 2–4 seeds. Ruellia humilis: R. humilis also has axillary nearly sessile flowers but is conspicuously long-pilose, especially on stems and leaf margins. Ruellia metziae: R. metziae also has terminal pedunculate flowers but is typically white to pale purple and has somewhat narrower leaves; preserve as a later local comparison.
